title: Long-context attention's quadratic cost
bottleneck: Standard attention scales quadratically with sequence length — doubling context quadruples compute — which makes million-token contexts astronomically expensive even before memory limits bite. Linear-attention alternatives exist but consistently underperform full attention on the hardest reasoning tasks, forcing a choice between affordable context and capable reasoning that nobody has resolved. This forces painful tradeoffs: shorter contexts, weaker models, or bills that scale superlinearly with every added token.
why_it_blocks: The most valuable applications need both long context and strong reasoning; the quadratic tax makes that combination the most expensive workload in AI.
current_state: Hybrid architectures and sparse attention narrow the gap; no linear alternative matches full attention on frontier reasoning benchmarks. KV-cache compression and eviction policies cut memory, but the underlying quadratic compute cost persists.
